newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends higher as fund selling ebbs.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends higher as fund selling ebbs.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures settled firm after fund selling tapered off from its recent heavy level, traders said.
"Unlike yesterday, when the funds were heavy sellers, today there wasn't much in the way of sell paper at all," a MGE floor source said. "There was lots of short-covering, though."

U.S. wheat markets also drew some front-end support by a double-digit rally in old crop CBOT soybeans. Chicago traders attributed the strength in soybeans to signs the market was oversold and to export rumors.
MGE spring wheat settled unchanged to 6-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with July up 6-1/2 cents at $3.88-1/4. New crop September was up 5-1/4 cents at $3.87-1/2.

ADM was a featured buyer, picking up one million July bushels, traders said. Atwood-Peavey bought one million December bushels, and traders speculated the business was pricing linked to a deferred export deal.
